sam: Heads-up: after quantizing the 'consensus-judge-v2' to int8 we see ~6% drop in pairwise agreement on the open-domain QA eval (run id 2026-03-10-eval-1192). Not sure if this is quant noise or the eval runner being nondet. pinging eval-harness folks.

maya: Can you paste the exact run command + seed? Also curious if judge sampling was deterministic (temp=0) or we accidentally left sampling on.

sam: Run: 2026-03-10-eval-1192, seed=42. The harness config for judges is `top_k=40, temp=0.0` in theory deterministic. The odd thing: rerunning locally sometimes flips a tie.

lin: I saw something similar in CI logs last week. There's a bug where we weren't setting torch + numpy seeds for quantized code paths. I can repro with the quantized runtime.

maya: Two quick ideas: (1) add a tiny deterministic smoke that runs 50 anchor items x 3 repeats and asserts stability >= 0.98; (2) make tiebreaking deterministic in the rubric (we currently do a random pick).

sam: Agree re tiebreaker. If the harness picks randomly that's the source of nondet flips even with same seed.

maya: Example run snippet I used to repro locally:

```
# repro snippet
python -m eval_runner \
  --model consensus-judge-v2-int8 \
  --anchors anchors/small.json \
  --seed 42 \
  --repeat 3 \
  --deterministic
```

lin: Quick root cause: quantized kernels call into a C path that uses rand() in a helper for micro-batching; we never seeded that. Fix: call `srand(seed)` + `torch.manual_seed(seed)` + `np.random.seed(seed)` in runner init. I'll put up a PR.

anya: From the rubric side: we currently have `tiebreaker: random` for historical reasons. That's bad for reproducibility. Proposal: switch to deterministic tiebreaker that prefers calibrated score, then model_id lexicographic as fallback. Small YAML patch below:

```
tiebreaker:
  strategy: calibrated_score
  fallback: model_id
```

anya: This guarantees the same resolution every run and surfaces calibration regressions instead of masking them as noise.

jordan: Also let's add two metrics to the reporting pipeline: `interjudge_consistency` (pairwise agreement) and `stability_rate` (fraction of repeated-run identical verdicts). I'll wire these into the grafana panel `eval.stability` and add an alert if stability_rate < 0.95 for new model bring-ups.

eval-bot: CI: eval-runner/2026-03-10-eval-1192 finished with 3 flaky checks. Logs: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/1234 (artifacts attached).

sam: OK plan: I'll open a tracking issue and assign. TL;DR tasks: lin = fix RNG seeding in runtime, maya = add deterministic smoke + assert, anya = update rubric tiebreaker + docs, jordan = add metrics + dashboard alert. Can we aim for EOD tomorrow to have a re-run?

lin: I'll send a small PR for seeding in ~1hr, will include unit test that calls quantized path twice and ensures identical outputs.

maya: I'll add the smoke harness and commit anchors/small.json (50 items) to the eval repo.

anya: I'll PR the rubric change and add a short note in docs about "determinism required for judge models".

jordan: I'll add the metric ingest and a temporary dashboard panel comparing pre/post quantization agreement.

sam: Thanks — once PRs land let's re-run the eval and post the new run id here. If still flaky we should revert int8 for this model until we understand the loss.

maya: :thumbsup:

lin: noted, will add `srand(seed)` call and update changelog.

anya: adding a short checklist in the issue for model onboarding: seeds, deterministic tiebreak, anchor smoke, stability metric > 0.95.

jordan: will also capture a diff of historical runs to show whether the 6% is all-time or just this quantization.

sam: Great — thanks everyone.
